summary: The notebooks of Lorenzo Scardicchio: essays and artwork, typeset like a book. Design language after the Stripe Press Poor Charlie's Almanack web edition: paper, ink, mono running heads, framed figure collages, unrolling parchment preambles, and dark Previous/Next chapter spreads.

steps.title: The book, page by page
steps.body: Essays and artwork by Lorenzo Scardicchio: the home opens the latest chapter (The Algorithmic Self, chapter 14, May 26, 2026, a seven-minute read), and each essay is a chapter with its opening, its collage and its dark Previous/Next spread.
steps.source: the home page's own words (photographed 2026-10-22); README

steps.title: The gallery wall
steps.body: A fixed, full-viewport surface you drag in any direction; on release the wall glides on and slows. Tiles are squares, each showing the work twice: the white cast always visible, the painting fading in on hover; cell (col, row) shows work ((col + row·K) mod n), so a window a few tiles wide never repeats a work side by side. Click a tile and the painting travels from its tile to the centre while a sheet slides in from the right; Escape, the veil or the painting itself close it, and the address follows.
steps.alt: The gallery wall: square tiles of white casts in a lattice.

steps.title: A chapter
steps.body: The Algorithmic Self: how AI is reshaping human identity, introspection, and agency. The chapter opening blurs and fades out over the first viewport, the collage drifts, the parchment preamble unrolls, and the reading progress runs along the bottom.
steps.alt: The opening of The Algorithmic Self: the title and subtitle on the paper, the running head above.
steps.source: the chapter's own title and subtitle; README (Scroll system)

steps.title: On a phone
steps.body: The home and a chapter on a phone; the wall shows two tiles across, and an opened painting sits above a sheet that rises from the bottom.

steps.title: The content pipeline
steps.body: Every public post is pulled from lorenzoscardicchio.substack.com and re-serialized into well-formed markup, its images localized; the artwork is curated from lorenzoscardicchio.com by an allow-list of named originals into the artwork manifest (painting, design, photo, logo).

Every word is qwarter.com's, the site's own or observed; nothing is written here. By hand (content/studies/_overrides/bambino.json): the words are the repository's own (journeynudger/bambino README.md, read 2026-10-22) and the site's (its home page and chapters, photographed from bambino-1dtu.vercel.app on 2026-10-22); the address is the one the README names as live (bambino-five.vercel.app). Named "Painter" at Lorenzo's word (2026-10-23).
brief: One scroll engine drives the book: a chapter opening blurs and fades over the first viewport, collages drift upward at staggered speeds, parchment panels unroll as the roll cylinder travels down, figures rise with a cosine ease as they enter, and a reading-progress bar runs along the bottom. The gallery is a wall: a fixed, full-viewport surface, an endless lattice of square tiles moved with a drag that glides on, each tile holding the work twice, the white cast always visible and the painting fading in under the hand. Opening a work sends the painting from its tile to the centre of the screen while a sheet slides in from the right.
